validity.recommendation: Human de-dup: merge P6023 (20") and P6022 (30") into ONE Esfarayen–Neqab–Joghatai entry (or two clearly-differentiated diameter segments of one ProjectID), not two identically-named ProjectIDs; check P6024 (10" Esfarayen branch) and P6025 (Sabzevar Steel spur) as the same source's other pieces.
validity.researcher_notes: P6023 and P6022 carry the EXACT same pipeline name ("Esfarayen–Neqab–Joghatai Gas Pipeline"), share the same gem.wiki page, and are both sourced SOLELY to one contractor project-directory listing (Iran Ertebat, iranertebat.com — the only outbound citation on the wiki page, 12 backlinks; P6024 cites the same page, 5 backlinks). That single listing describes ONE combined project: a reinforcing gas transmission line of BOTH 30-inch AND 20-inch pipe, total ~70 km, Esfarayen–Neqab–Joghatai, Razavi/North Khorasan, built to supply Sabzevar Steel Plant and to strengthen the existing 10-inch Esfarayen branch. GEM has split that one project across at least three ProjectIDs: P6022 = the 30" leg (len 48), P6023 = the 20" leg (len 35, "Expansion 2"), P6024 = the pre-existing 10" Esfarayen branch the same text says is being reinforced. 48+35=83 km vs the source's stated combined 70 km. This is a segment/relabel double-count of a single physical reinforcing corridor, not two independent pipelines. The line is REAL (contractor documents having built it) and correctly a gas transmission line, so this is not a phantom — but the duplication/segmentation and the reliance on a single now-dead source are the material problems. No GulfPub counterpart exists (GulfPub PE World Map covers only major Iranian trunks; a provincial reinforcing line is legitimately absent), so no independent corroboration is available there either.

validity.recommendation: Change Owner from 'National Iranian Oil Co' (NIOC) to National Iranian Gas Company (NIGC) / its transmission arm; and correct StartState/Province from 'Razavi Khorasan' to 'North Khorasan' (Esfarayen is in North Khorasan; the line crosses into Razavi Khorasan at Joveyn/Neqab and Joghatai).
validity.researcher_notes: Owner is listed as 'National Iranian Oil Co' (NIOC, 100%). NIOC is the upstream oil company; an intra-provincial gas transmission/reinforcing line feeding a steel plant and city network is an NIGC (National Iranian Gas Company) / provincial-gas-transmission asset, built here by contractor Iran Ertebat under an NIGC/Khorasan-Razavi Gas Co scope. Owner attribution to NIOC is very likely wrong. Separately, the sheet puts both endpoints' province as 'Razavi Khorasan', but Esfarayen (the named start) is in NORTH Khorasan province and borders Sabzevar County to the south — confirmed via independent geography (Wikipedia: Esfarayen, North Khorasan). Neqab (capital of Joveyn County) and Joghatai are in Razavi Khorasan. So the start-province value is wrong; the line is a two-province corridor.

routes.corridor_desc: Reinforcing gas transmission corridor running south from Esfarayen (North Khorasan) across the county line into the Joveyn plain of Razavi Khorasan, through Neqab (Joveyn county seat) and on to Joghatai, ultimately reinforcing supply toward Sabzevar Steel Plant. Total combined 20"+30" project ~70 km per the sole (dead) source; this 20" leg is one portion. Endpoint coordinates are town centroids from independent geography (Wikipedia), NOT a surveyed pipe route — the exact alignment through the Joveyn plain is not published, so the corridor is bounded loosely by the three named towns. Note the town order in the name (Esfarayen–Neqab–Joghatai) is roughly N-to-S/SW; Neqab (~57.55E) sits east of Joghatai (~57.07E), so the physical order Esfarayen→Neqab→Joghatai implies a westward turn across the plain rather than a straight line.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints established from the pipeline name plus independent Wikipedia coordinates for the three named towns: Esfarayen 37.07056N 57.50556E (North Khorasan), Joghatai 36.63833N 57.07167E (Razavi Khorasan), Neqab/Joveyn County ~36.617N 57.55E. All three URLs verified OK via url_verifier. No coordinates fabricated: the intermediate alignment is unsurveyed, so only named-town centroids are given and the route between them is described in words. Corridor keeps current 'medium' accuracy — endpoints are known but exact pipe path is not.

summary: P6023 is a real, correctly-classed gas transmission line but is one diameter-leg (20", 35km) of a SINGLE Iran Ertebat reinforcing project split across P6022(30")/P6023(20")/P6024(10") under identical names on one now-dead source — duplicate/segmentation + attribution(NIOC→NIGC, start province North not Razavi Khorasan) + spec(35km split unverified; only combined ~70km attested; FuelSource 'Esfarayen' dubious) concerns.
